text.p: Sudan denied on Saturday Ugandan charges that it twice bombed targets in northern Uganda.

Culture and Information Minister Brigadier al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohammed Khair said in the government-owned al-Ingaz al-Watani that the charges were baseless and that they could be designed to "escalate the military situation in the area".
Sudan has said Uganda has massed troops on the border in preparation for launching an attack on Sudan.

Uganda's Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi said in a statement on Friday that an Antonov transport plane, which Khartoum uses as a bomber, and a MiG jet violated Ugandan airspace late on Thursday afternoon.
"They tried to bomb Moyo army barracks but missed the target. Three civilians and one child were injured. Five bombs which fell near the barracks did not explode," Mbabazi said.

"Later last night at about nine o'clock another military aircraft of Antonov type again entered from Sudan via Koboko and Arua and dropped bombs, wounding one person seriously and three other persons sustaining minor injuries," he added.
He said Ugandan army anti-aircraft batteries fired at the Sudanese planes but they were out of range.
The Ugandan government last accused a Sudanese plane of violating its airspace on February 3.
Independent sources have confirmed Sudanese planes have bombed northern Uganda several times in the past two years but Khartoum denies doing so or says the attacks were unintentional.
Khartoum accuses Uganda of backing the Sudan People's Liberation Army, which has been fighting since 1983 in the mainly Christian and animist south against the Moslem and Arabised north.
In turn, Uganda says Sudan supports rebel movements in northern and western Uganda. Both countries deny the charges.
